text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 2.85% today, continuing a sharp two-week rally that's gained over 20% since early October. The refining industry has been a beneficiary of tightening diesel supplies and elevated global oil prices—Brent crude topped $106 earlier this week after geopolitical disruptions, and U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% capacity to meet strong demand. As a major U.S. refiner, Marathon profits when crude costs less relative to the refined products it sells, especially when diesel commands a premium due to supply constraints.

The near-term backdrop remains volatile but supportive for refiners. While oil prices have pulled back slightly today as traders weigh competing supply stories—potential Russian diesel entering markets versus ongoing Middle East tensions from the Saudi-Houthi conflict—U.S. refinery utilization stays elevated and diesel storage remains relatively lean at 105 million barrels. That combination of steady run rates and tight product supplies is exactly what keeps refiner margins resilient in an environment of geopolitical uncertainty.
